Read and normalise a NONMEM-like dataset

Source: R/nm_read_csv.R
nm_read_csv.Rd

Read and normalise a NONMEM-like dataset

Usage

nm_read_csv(
  file,
  sep = ",",
  na = c("", "NA", "."),
  time_unit = c("h", "d"),
  lloq = NULL,
  blq_col = NULL,
  date_format = NULL,
  dv_col = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

file

Path to the CSV file.

sep

Column separator (default ",").

na

Strings to be treated as missing values.

time_unit

Output unit for TIME: "h" (default) or "d".

lloq

LLOQ value. If supplied and no BLQ/CENS column exists, records with DV < lloq are flagged as BLQ.

blq_col

Name of the BLQ flag column (1 = BLQ, 0 = quantified). By default, "BLQ" or "CENS" is auto-detected.

date_format

Date format forced in lubridate::parse_date_time() (e.g. "dmy" for DD/MM/YYYY). By default, chosen from the name of the DATE/DAT1-3 column.

dv_col

Name of the DV column if non-standard (e.g. "DV_nmol/L"). If NULL (default), a column whose name starts with "DV" is auto-detected. Required when several DV columns exist.

verbose

Print the identification report (default TRUE).

Value

A list:

  • data: data.frame with relative TIME, BLQ (logical), and DV_norm when AMT is available. Reserved columns are renamed in upper case.

  • mapping: reserved labels -> original column names.

  • lloq: LLOQ value used (NULL if not supplied).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- nm_read_csv("data.csv", lloq = 0.5)
head(res$data)
} # }
